---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: CashBackedDurableEarnings
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 5), NEG(VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms whose reported profits carry low accrual content AND whose cash earnings are high and stable over five years have genuinely cash-backed, repeatable performance that the market under-prices relative to firms with equally high headline earnings.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Low accruals alone can reflect transitory cash timing, while stable high cash earnings alone can be capitalized already; the joint rank requires the cash-flow level to be durable and the earnings-to-cash gap to be small. Combining three ranked channels (accrual content, cash-earnings level, earnings instability) isolates the "durable cash earnings" state rather than either theme in isolation.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: AccrualSignalGatedByNoLossHistory
EXPRESSION: MUL(NEG(ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1))), INDICATOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(ib, at), 5), 0))
HYPOTHESIS: The accrual anomaly is concentrated in firms with persistently profitable (never-loss) earnings histories, because for chronically unprofitable or erratic firms the accrual measure is dominated by write-offs and noise rather than by earnings-quality information.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The indicator turns the accrual z-score on only when minimum five-year ROA is positive, setting all low-persistence firms to a neutral zero so they neither lengthen nor short the spread. This is a genuine conditional interaction: the quality state determines whether accruals carry information, not merely an additive tilt.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: CashEarningsPerUnitAccountingNoise
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(MA(RATIO(oancf, at), 5), ADD(ABS(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)), VOL(RATIO(ib, at), 5))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: A signal-to-noise ratio of profitability — average operating cash return divided by combined accrual magnitude and earnings volatility — identifies firms whose profits are economically real, and such firms earn higher subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The numerator is the durable cash component of profitability while the denominator aggregates the two sources of accounting noise (large accrual wedges and unstable earnings), so the ratio is high only when a solid cash return is delivered with minimal accrual distortion. This scaled form makes the interaction multiplicative rather than additive, penalizing high cash return that arrives with heavy accrual or volatility baggage.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: AccrualNoiseDominatesCashFlow
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(VOL(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5), ADD(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5), MA(ABS(RATIO(oancf, at)), 5))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: When the volatility of the accrual wedge is large relative to the volatility and scale of operating cash flows, reported earnings are driven by accounting discretion (smoothing or aggressive recognition) rather than economics, forecasting poor subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The construct compares second moments across the two themes: accrual variability (accruals theme) benchmarked against cash-flow variability and cash-flow scale (quality theme), which is exactly the smoothing/manipulation diagnostic that a single-theme accrual level cannot capture. High values flag firms whose earnings series is manufactured by accruals, and these should underperform genuinely cash-driven peers.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: ImprovingAccrualsRisingCashTrend
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 1)), SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(oancf, at), 5), NEG(VOL(RATIO(oancf, at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: A contraction in the accrual wedge that coincides with a rising and steady operating cash-flow trend signals a real, cash-validated improvement in fundamentals, whereas a falling accrual wedge alone can simply reflect reversal of prior overstatement.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is a change-based interaction: the accrual channel is a first difference and the quality channel is a five-year trend plus stability of cash returns, so only firms where cash flow is genuinely catching up to (or exceeding) earnings score high. It separates cash-confirmed fundamental improvement from mechanical accrual mean reversion.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: WorkingCapitalAccrualsVsRetainedProfitability
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(NEG(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(wcap, 1), dp), at))), IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(re, at), RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at))))
HYPOTHESIS: Low balance-sheet (working-capital minus depreciation) accruals combined with a long record of accumulated profitability and high gross margins identify firms whose conservative accounting rests on a durable earnings franchise, and these firms outperform.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Retained earnings over assets is a cumulative measure of realized, non-manipulable past profit, so pairing it with low current working-capital accruals distinguishes structurally profitable conservative accounters from marginal firms that happen to report small accruals. Industry-relative ranking on both legs removes sector differences in working-capital intensity and margin norms, keeping the interaction rather than an industry bet.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
